value: This article provides a comprehensive overview of toposes, fundamental mathematical structures that generalize the category of sets and categories of sheaves. Defined either by their rich internal categorical properties (such as having finite limits and power objects, characterizing elementary toposes) or as categories of sheaves on a site (Grothendieck toposes), toposes offer a powerful and versatile framework. They are significant for possessing an internal intuitionistic higher-order logic, enabling a broad range of mathematical reasoning within their structure, and for acting as "generalized spaces" that extend classical topological concepts. The article details their various definitions, properties, types of morphisms, diverse examples (including higher toposes), and wide-ranging applications, illustrating their unifying role across different mathematical disciplines.
